questions.prompt: A population has mean \(50\) and standard deviation \(12\). For \(n=64\) independent observations, approximate the distribution of the sample mean.
questions.answer: By the central limit theorem, \(\bar X\) is approximately normal for a large independent sample. Its mean is \(50\), and its standard error is \(12/\sqrt{64}=1.5\), so \(\bar X\approx N(50,1.5^2)\).

questions.prompt: A skewed population has mean \(20\) and standard deviation \(5\). Let \(S_{100}\) be the sum of \(100\) independent observations. Use the central limit theorem to estimate \(P(S_{100}>2100)\).
questions.answer: For a sum, the CLT gives \(S_{100}\approx N(100\cdot20,100\cdot5^2)\), so the mean is \(2000\) and the standard deviation is \(5\sqrt{100}=50\). The z-score is \((2100-2000)/50=2\), hence \[P(S_{100}>2100)\approx1-\Phi(2)=1-0.9772=0.0228.\]

questions.prompt: A non-normal population has mean \(10\) and standard deviation \(3\). For a total of \(36\) independent observations, approximate \(P(S_{36}<324)\).
questions.answer: The CLT gives \(S_{36}\approx N(36\cdot10,36\cdot3^2)\). Thus \(E(S_{36})=360\) and \(\operatorname{sd}(S_{36})=3\sqrt{36}=18\). The z-score is \((324-360)/18=-2\), so \[P(S_{36}<324)\approx\Phi(-2)=0.0228.\]

questions.prompt: A machine output has mean \(8\) and standard deviation \(2\). For \(49\) independent outputs, approximate \(P(\bar X>8.4)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(2/\sqrt{49}=0.2857\). The z-score is \((8.4-8)/0.2857=1.40\), so \[P(\bar X>8.4)\approx1-\Phi(1.40)\approx1-0.9192=0.0808.\]

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(4\) and standard deviation \(6\). For \(n=225\), approximate the distribution of the total \(S_n\).
questions.answer: For totals, the CLT gives \(S_n\approx N(n\mu,n\sigma^2)\). Here \(E(S_n)=225(4)=900\) and \(\operatorname{sd}(S_n)=\sqrt{225}(6)=90\), so \(S_n\approx N(900,90^2)\).

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(30\) and standard deviation \(6\). For \(n=144\), estimate \(P(S_n<3720)\), where \(S_n\) is the sample total.
questions.answer: The total has approximate mean \(144(30)=4320\) and standard deviation \(\sqrt{144}(6)=72\). The z-score is \((3720-4320)/72=-8.33\). A standard normal table has essentially no mass this far into the left tail; for example it is far below \(z=-3.99\), where \(\Phi(z)<0.0001\). Thus \(P(S_n<3720)\approx0.0000\) to four decimal places.

questions.prompt: A waiting time distribution is strongly skewed with mean \(5\) minutes and standard deviation \(4\) minutes. Explain why \(\bar X\) for \(n=100\) can still be approximated by a normal distribution.
questions.answer: The individual observations need not be normal. The CLT says that, for a large independent sample with finite variance, the sampling distribution of \(\bar X\) is approximately normal. Here \(n=100\) is large, so the approximation is reasonable.

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(75\) and standard deviation \(15\). For \(n=900\), estimate \(P(\bar X>76)\).
questions.answer: The standard error is \(15/\sqrt{900}=0.5\). The z-score is \((76-75)/0.5=2\). Thus \[P(\bar X>76)\approx1-\Phi(2)=0.0228.\]

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(100\) and standard deviation \(30\). For \(n=400\), estimate \(P(99<\bar X<101)\).
A total \(S_{64}\) is formed from independent observations with mean \(12\) and standard deviation \(4\). Approximate \(P(S_{64}>800)\).
questions.answer: The approximate mean is \(64(12)=768\) and standard deviation is \(\sqrt{64}(4)=32\). The z-score is \((800-768)/32=1\), so \[P(S_{64}>800)\approx1-\Phi(1)=0.1587.\]

questions.prompt: A population has finite mean \(0\) and finite standard deviation \(10\). What happens to the standard error of \(\bar X\) when \(n\) changes from \(25\) to \(100\)?
questions.answer: The standard error is \(\sigma/\sqrt n\). It changes from \(10/5=2\) to \(10/10=1\). Quadrupling the sample size halves the standard error.

questions.prompt: A non-normal population has mean \(200\) and standard deviation \(24\). A sample of \(36\) observations is taken. Estimate the probability that the total is below \(7056\).
questions.answer: The total has approximate mean \(36(200)=7200\) and standard deviation \(24\sqrt{36}=144\). The z-score is \((7056-7200)/144=-1\), so \[P(S_{36}<7056)\approx\Phi(-1)=0.1587.\]

questions.prompt: A sample total from \(n=100\) independent claims has individual mean \(40\) and standard deviation \(25\). Estimate \(P(S_{100}>4250)\).
A population has mean \(6\), standard deviation \(9\), and a very skewed distribution. Which sample size, \(n=4\) or \(n=100\), gives a more reliable CLT approximation for \(\bar X\), and why?
questions.answer: The sample size \(n=100\) gives the more reliable approximation. The CLT is an asymptotic result: as \(n\) grows, the sampling distribution of \(\bar X\) becomes closer to normal, especially when the original population is skewed.

questions.prompt: Independent service times have mean \(3\) minutes and standard deviation \(2\) minutes. Approximate the probability that \(50\) services take less than \(140\) minutes in total.
A highly skewed delivery-time distribution has mean \(18\) minutes and standard deviation \(12\) minutes. For \(64\) deliveries, estimate \(P(1024<S_{64}<1280)\), where \(S_{64}\) is the total time.
questions.answer: The CLT gives \(S_{64}\approx N(64\cdot18,(12\sqrt{64})^2)\), so the mean is \(1152\) and the standard deviation is \(96\). The z-scores are \((1024-1152)/96=-1.33\) and \((1280-1152)/96=1.33\). Therefore \[P(1024<S_{64}<1280)\approx0.9082-0.0918=0.8164.\]

questions.prompt: A sample total \(S_n\) has \(n=400\), individual mean \(2.5\), and individual standard deviation \(1.2\). Estimate \(P(S_n>1024)\).
questions.answer: The total has mean \(400(2.5)=1000\) and standard deviation \(\sqrt{400}(1.2)=24\). The z-score is \((1024-1000)/24=1\), so \[P(S_n>1024)\approx0.1587.\]

questions.prompt: A batch total \(S_{900}\) is formed from independent observations with mean \(120\) and standard deviation \(60\). Use the CLT to estimate \(P(S_{900}>109800)\).
questions.answer: The total has approximate mean \(900(120)=108000\) and standard deviation \(60\sqrt{900}=1800\). The z-score is \((109800-108000)/1800=1\), so \[P(S_{900}>109800)\approx1-\Phi(1)=0.1587.\]

questions.prompt: A heavy-tailed population has finite variance. State two assumptions needed before using the CLT for an average.
questions.answer: The observations should be independent and identically distributed, or close enough for the model, and the variance should be finite. A sufficiently large \(n\) is also needed so that the normal approximation is accurate.

questions.prompt: A population has mean \(10\) and standard deviation \(5\). Find the sample size needed so that the CLT approximation for the total \(S_n\) has standard deviation \(50\).
questions.answer: For a total, \(\operatorname{sd}(S_n)=\sigma\sqrt n\). Set \(5\sqrt n=50\). Then \(\sqrt n=10\), so \(n=100\). This is a CLT total calculation, not a standard-error calculation for \(\bar X\).
